s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic gastrointestinal symptoms with malabsorption and dermatological manifestations
salient_findings: Brownish macules on the hands and feet
Hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk
key_facts: History of cleft lip and palate repair
Multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
Nodular lymphoid lesions in the duodenum
Numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic gastrointestinal symptoms with malabsorption and dermatological manifestations
salient_findings: Brownish macules on the hands and feet
Hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk
key_facts: History of cleft lip and palate repair
Multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
Nodular lymphoid lesions in the duodenum
Numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

shortlist.label: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple polyps throughout the colon and rectum, and dermatological manifestations

shortlist.label: Juvenile polyposis syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

shortlist.label: Celiac disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic gastrointestinal symptoms with malabsorption and dermatological manifestations

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic diarrhea, weight loss, and abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Autoimmune enteropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent diarrheal episodes since childhood and autoimmune manifestations

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum, along with the patient's history of recurrent diarrheal episodes since childhood and significant weight loss, supports this diagnosis. The findings of multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa and nodular lymphoid lesions in the duodenum further align with juvenile polyposis syndrome.

rejected.label: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
rejected.why: While it involves polyps, the characteristic mucocutaneous melanin deposits and specific polyp distribution are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Celiac disease
rejected.why: The presence of atrophic gastric mucosa and the specific types of polyps found do not align with celiac disease, which primarily affects the small intestine and does not typically present with such polyp formations.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: The lack of specific findings such as skip lesions, deep ulcers, or cobblestone appearance in the colonoscopy results, which are more characteristic of Crohn's disease, makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Autoimmune enteropathy
rejected.why: While autoimmune enteropathy can present with diarrhea and malabsorption, the prominent feature of numerous polyps throughout the colon and rectum is not typical for this condition.
